newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open barely changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open barely changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open barely changed Wednesday, floor sources said.
Activity is expected to remain confined to a range between the contract high of 11.75 cents a lb hit Tuesday and 11.60 cents for the October contract.
A move below support could trigger sell stops that are rumored to be resting around 11.57 cents and pressure the spot month to its next downside target of 11.55 to 11.50 cents, traders said.

Tuesday, most-active October closed off 0.04 cent at 11.66 cents after trading from a new contract high of 11.75 cents to 11.61 cents. Second-position March settled 0.09 lower at 11.86 cents, while the rest finished down 0.05 and 0.06 cent.
An estimated 19,668 lots changed hands on the day.
In fundamental news, Kenya said sugar output would rise to 462,000 tonnes in 1997 and 485,000 tonnes in 1998. Kenya produced 420,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996.

Eastern Europe's beet crop is expected to progress normally despite recent heavy rains in Poland, Slovakia and the Czech Republic, statitician F.O. Licht said. The crop is expected to benefit from dry weather forecast for the next two weeks.
LIFFE October white sugar futures were barely lower in light trade Wednesday. At 0840 EDT/1240 GMT, the spot month stood 30 cents lower at $328.00.
